scheme_name: Documentation of Tiatr through Research Work
description:
The "Documentation of Tiatr through Research Work" scheme was launched by the Government of Goa in 2021. 

This initiative aims to preserve and promote the rich cultural heritage of Tiatr, which is a traditional form of musical theatre in Goa. 

Tiatr has a significant historical context, having evolved from the 19th century under Portuguese colonial influence. 

The scheme recognizes the need to document this unique art form to ensure its survival and appreciation among future generations. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to conduct comprehensive research on Tiatr. 

The government aims to compile a detailed repository of information that includes scripts, performances, and the history of Tiatr. 

The target is to document at least 100 Tiatr scripts by the end of the first phase of the project. 

The timeline for this initial phase is set for two years, starting from its launch in 2021. 

The scheme also aims to promote awareness about Tiatr among the youth and encourage their participation in this art form. 

Benefits of this scheme include financial assistance for researchers and artists involved in the documentation process. 

Each researcher can receive up to INR 50,000 as a grant for their work. 

Additionally, artists participating in workshops and training sessions can receive stipends of INR 5,000 per month. 

Eligibility criteria for researchers include a minimum educational qualification of a bachelor's degree in arts or a related field. 

Researchers must also demonstrate a strong interest in Goan culture and the performing arts. 

Artists who wish to participate must be at least 18 years old and have prior experience in Tiatr. 

The application process for this scheme involves several steps. 

Interested researchers must submit a detailed proposal outlining their research objectives and methodology. 

Proposals should also include a timeline for the completion of the research work. 

Applications must be submitted to the Department of Art and Culture, Government of Goa. 

Required documents include proof of educational qualifications, a curriculum vitae, and any previous work samples related to Tiatr. 

The deadline for submitting applications is typically set for the end of March each year. 

Once applications are reviewed, selected candidates will be notified by the end of April. 

Disbursement of funds occurs in two installments. 

The first installment is released upon approval of the proposal, while the second is provided upon submission of the final report. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Art and Culture, Government of Goa. 

The department is responsible for overseeing the research work and ensuring that documentation adheres to the set guidelines. 

Contact details for the Department of Art and Culture can be found on the official Goa government website. 

The scheme also includes collaboration with local Tiatr troupes and cultural organizations. 

Workshops and training sessions are organized to enhance the skills of participants. 

These sessions focus on scriptwriting, acting, and stage management. 

The government aims to conduct at least 10 workshops annually under this scheme. 

Each workshop can accommodate up to 30 participants. 

The documentation process will also involve recording oral histories from veteran Tiatr artists. 

This aspect is crucial for capturing the nuances and traditions that may not be available in written form. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 1 crore for the entire project over the two-year period. 

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme will be conducted every six months. 

Feedback from participants will be collected to improve future iterations of the program. 

The scheme also aims to create a digital archive of documented materials. 

This archive will be accessible to the public and serve as a resource for researchers and enthusiasts. 

The long-term goal is to establish Tiatr as an integral part of Goa's cultural identity. 

The government plans to organize an annual Tiatr festival to showcase the documented works. 

This festival will provide a platform for new artists and encourage the revival of traditional performances. 

The first festival is scheduled to take place in December 2023. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from the local community and cultural organizations. 

Many believe that it will help in reviving interest in Tiatr among younger generations. 

The initiative aligns with the broader goals of the Government of Goa to promote cultural heritage and tourism. 

By documenting Tiatr, the government aims to enhance its visibility on national and international platforms. 

This scheme is part of a larger effort to support the arts and culture sector in Goa. 

The government recognizes the economic potential of cultural tourism and aims to leverage Tiatr for this purpose. 

In conclusion, the "Documentation of Tiatr through Research Work" scheme represents a significant step towards preserving Goa's cultural heritage. 

Through targeted research and community involvement, the initiative seeks to ensure that Tiatr continues to thrive in the years to come. 

The scheme not only provides financial support but also fosters a sense of community among artists and researchers. 

It is a vital effort to keep the spirit of Tiatr alive for future generations. 

This initiative reflects the commitment of the Government of Goa to promote and protect its unique cultural identity. 

As the scheme progresses, it is expected to yield valuable insights into the evolution of Tiatr and its impact on Goan society. 

The documentation efforts will contribute to a greater understanding of this art form and its significance in the cultural landscape of India. 

Overall, the scheme is a comprehensive approach to safeguarding the legacy of Tiatr through research and community engagement.
